questiontext.text: What structure does the Composite pattern compose objects into?

answer.text: A tree structure representing part-whole hierarchies
A single global instance with a global access point
A chain of wrappers each adding responsibilities
An adapter converting one interface into another

generalfeedback.text: Composite composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies.

questiontext.text: Into which GoF category does Composite fall?

answer.text: Structural

feedback.text: Correct — Composite is a structural pattern about how objects are composed.

answer.text: Creational

feedback.text: No — creational patterns concern object creation.

answer.text: Behavioral

feedback.text: No — behavioral patterns concern communication and responsibility.

generalfeedback.text: Composite is a structural pattern, alongside Adapter and Decorator.

questiontext.text: What key benefit does Composite provide to client code?

answer.text: Clients can treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly

feedback.text: Correct — uniform treatment of leaves and composites is the point.

answer.text: It guarantees a class has exactly one instance
It converts an incompatible interface into an expected one

generalfeedback.text: Because leaves and composites share one interface, clients can ignore the difference between a single object and a group.

questiontext.text: What do leaf and composite nodes share in the Composite pattern?

answer.text: A common component interface

feedback.text: Correct — both implement one common interface so clients treat them uniformly.

answer.text: A single shared instance created by a static accessor
A Director that sequences their construction

generalfeedback.text: Leaf and composite classes both implement a common component interface, enabling uniform treatment.
